Since the schema file is being dropped, you should delete lines 84-90 here.

If I'm understanding things correctly, the file format currently consists of two JSON object types: ChassisPowerMonitor and GPIO.

You might consider simplifying the first JSON object type name to just Chassis, since each one represents properties of a chassis.

The outermost part of the file format is an array of Chassis objects.
```
[
  Chassis,
  Chassis,
  Chassis
]
```

Each Chassis object has the properties you describe below. Most of them have a value of a GPIO object. That object type has properties too.

You can document both object types here + the overall config file format, but that might get a bit confusing. I would recommend creating chassis.md and gpio.md files that each cover one object type. You can give a description of the object, show the properties, and have an example at the bottom if you wish.

Then in the README you could state the overall format is an array of Chassis objects and put in a link to the chassis.md file for more information. The chassis.md would have a link to the gpio.md file next to the gpio properties.

See the phosphor-regulators or phosphor-power-sequencer docs/config_file directories for examples you can copy/paste.
Done

Just a nit, not worth re-doing the commit for just this, but in our systems the PresenceGpio will be "detected", and indicate true or false (0 or 1).  For other companies systems, if they don't even use that gpio, it won't be "detected".

Eg, if the PresenceGpio is detected but indicating "False", but the PresencePath is present/exists, then we should treat this as the chassis being present.

It might be a copy/paste from how EntityManager does JSON. I think the Name there is often used to form the D-Bus object path. Not sure if that is relevant here.

If there is no clear need, I'd vote for removing the property and just having the chassis number (ChassisID).

Since the GPIOs have a polarity, we probably need to say something like "If the GPIO value read from the chassis is 1 and the Polarity property is High, then it is present"?

@derekh@us.ibm.com I'm curious about the "detected" references in these sentences. If a GPIO property is defined in the JSON, then I assume being able to acquire and read the GPIO is required? And if we can't, then we'd log some sort of error? Or is there a detection phase too?

If there is no detection phase, then I'd think we could state it more like "If the PresenceGpio property is defined, then ...  If the PresencePath property is defined, ...  If both properties are defined, then ..."

Yes if we can't read the presence detect gpio, we should log an error.  Will likely be the generic i2c failure PEL. 

The main point is we should treat a chassis as missing just because there is an i2c fail trying to read it's presence; we should just say to replace the FRU causing the i2c fail, not say the whole chassis is missing and stop using it.
